bug_semantics: A tenant allowed to create or update Fission Function or Environment CRDs can put SYS_TIME in securityContext.capabilities.add on a tenant-controlled container or init container. The v1.24.0 admission validator and executor merge sanitizer reject only six named capabilities (SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, DAC_OVERRIDE), so SYS_TIME passes both layers and reaches the resulting pod. Without PSA restricted on the function-pod namespace, CAP_SYS_TIME permits clock_settime(CLOCK_REALTIME) against the node-wide, non-time-namespaced real-time clock, corrupting wall-clock-dependent state for co-tenants.
flaw_origin: Incomplete remediation: PR #3391 introduced a fixed six-capability denylist while closing earlier PodSpec privilege-escalation advisories. The first PR member, 2db76f65dbfe4f657b4a4efb506ed63b24623e92, created dangerousCapabilities and deliberately allowed every capability outside that enumeration; later member c8a58b7a88448f55bdf3ff01e149e82370fcfd7d copied the same incomplete policy into the merge sanitizer. The underlying unconstrained SecurityContext merge already existed in the parent, but this advisory's specific flawed mechanism is the newly written, incomplete denylist defense.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/fission/fission/security/advisories/GHSA-qf5v-m7p4-95rp states affected <=1.24.0, patched 1.25.0, the SYS_TIME path, and PR #3465 / 2569b42b as the fix. In the validated clone, `git show v1.24.0:pkg/apis/core/v1/podspec_safety.go` shows dangerousCapabilities contains exactly SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, DAC_OVERRIDE and ValidateContainerSafety rejects only map hits; `git show v1.24.0:pkg/executor/util/merge.go` shows the identical dangerousMergeContainerCapabilities map and sanitizer filter. `git grep -n -E 'ValidateContainerSafety|sanitizeContainerSecurityContext' v1.24.0 -- pkg/apis/core/v1 pkg/executor/util/merge.go` shows validation of PodSpec containers/initContainers and bare Environment runtime/builder containers plus sanitization at the merge sites. `git log -L 14,25:pkg/apis/core/v1/podspec_safety.go v1.24.0` and `git log -S dangerousCapabilities --all -- pkg/apis/core/v1/podspec_safety.go` identify landing squash e484df8460bb4e8026e24210120602aa7f181f64. GitHub's first-party PR commit endpoint https://api.github.com/repos/fission/fission/pulls/3391/commits decomposes that squash as 2db76f65dbfe4f657b4a4efb506ed63b24623e92 -> 1faffd464be7b4266c3e8dbbb17a11b9d5db53b8 -> c8a58b7a88448f55bdf3ff01e149e82370fcfd7d -> c9ed98a158d06876eadf179e4897fe9d0db5c3e8. The commit endpoint for 2db76f65dbfe4f657b4a4efb506ed63b24623e92 reports parent 8fa799417c77ce8a0189d9858bfe11ece29b84a6 and an added-file patch that creates dangerousCapabilities with the six entries and the reject-only-on-map-hit loop. `git show -s --format='%T' e484df8460bb4e8026e24210120602aa7f181f64` returns c83a8ef23becd9e5602a8e569de820d22c0fdd32, equal to c9ed98a1's tree from the PR API, proving the decomposition. Direct parent verification: `git cat-file -e 8fa799417c77ce8a0189d9858bfe11ece29b84a6:pkg/apis/core/v1/podspec_safety.go` fails because the file is absent; `git grep -n -E 'MergeContainer|WithOverride|ValidatePodSpecSafety' 8fa799417c77ce8a0189d9858bfe11ece29b84a6 -- pkg/executor/util/merge.go pkg/apis/core/v1/validation.go` finds mergo.WithOverride but no ValidatePodSpecSafety, confirming the pre-remediation passthrough and absence of the new flawed defense. The BIC API commit object names human author/committer Sanket Sudake and contains the exact Claude Co-Authored-By trailer quoted in ai_marker; no PR-body or later-commit signal is used. Fix verification: `git show 2569b42bfadbcb7d78b55a00a60f77937e522699 -- pkg/apis/core/v1/podspec_safety.go pkg/executor/util/merge.go` replaces both denylists with a NET_BIND_SERVICE-only allowlist and rejects/filters every non-member. https://api.github.com/repos/fission/fission/pulls/3465/commits identifies 943121151156b777a73bda8a7dee0a6bdd6efd8a as the direct member that first makes that change; the final PR-member tree 1226b159a47b6f5be4578b4304c5243e577f1b4b equals squash 2569b42b's tree. Tag checks resolve v1.24.0 to ce617120c41b9e4a51d577f81b441238264e88fd and v1.25.0 to ae970aaa9bc76ec93d748bdaf03fd7523b6b6a62; `git merge-base --is-ancestor e484df84 v1.24.0` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 2569b42b v1.25.0` succeed, while the fix-to-v1.24.0 ancestry check fails.
reasoning: The security property is not merely that some dangerous capabilities are named: every tenant-requestable capability outside an explicit safe set must be rejected before pod creation and removed on merge. PR #3391's first member wrote the authoritative denylist and its permissive complement, so it is the smallest commit that first wrote this case's flawed mechanism. The later c8a58b7a merge-layer member duplicated rather than originated the policy. The main-branch commit e484df84 is a squash aggregate and therefore is not the BIC; matching trees and the first-party PR commit chain permit decomposition to 2db76f65. The direct parent lacks the safety file and validator, although it already had the broader unsafe passthrough, making this lifecycle an AI-assisted incomplete remediation rather than the original creation of tenant PodSpec capability control. The v1.24.0 release contains the flawed squash. Direct fix member 94312115 changes both enforcement layers to an allowlist; its final effective PR state (after rollback of the incompatible forced drop:[ALL] step) landed as squash 2569b42b and is present in v1.25.0. Because the smallest BIC itself carries an explicit Claude co-author trailer and its own commit message expressly defines the denylist design that omitted SYS_TIME, commit-object attribution and causal code linkage are direct; under the audit definitions this is AI_ROOT_CAUSE for the incomplete-denylist mechanism.
